acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1761 first tell me what the issue is"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant explains what GitHub issue entireio/cli#1761 reports (the Codex hook trust check misses single-quoted TOML state keys, producing a false 'REVIEW NEEDED'), using the issue when reachable, or saying it cannot be reached and explaining from what the repository shows.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "trace through code for me please"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant traces the code path behind the issue through the repository, identifying where the trust check runs (doctor and SessionStart call sites) and where the hooks.state keys are read from config.toml.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 1: "can you implement this and then sandbox test this? just asking? ultrathink and tell me first"
acceptance_criteria.text: In response to turn 1, the assistant presents a plan explaining whether and how it would implement the fix and sandbox-test it.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 1: "just asking? ... tell me first" — the user asked to be told before anything is done
acceptance_criteria.text: No repository files are edited in response to turn 1; changes begin only after the user's go-ahead in turn 2.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 2 asked to try the fix in a Windows container, which implies implementing the fix for the issue the user referenced; the issue's reported defect is single-quoted keys being ignored.
acceptance_criteria.text: After the change, hooks declared in .codex/hooks.json whose approval is recorded in config.toml with single-quoted (TOML literal) hooks.state keys are recognized as trusted and produce no trust gaps.

acceptance_criteria.source: Implementing the issue's fix for Windows paths implies the trust check works for Windows-path keys in either TOML quoting form; the issue's proposed structural parse covers both.
acceptance_criteria.text: After the change, double-quoted hooks.state keys containing escaped Windows backslashes (e.g. "C:\\repo\\.codex\\hooks.json:...") are compared in unescaped form so they match the path the CLI builds for the hooks.json file.

acceptance_criteria.source: The change must not break the repository's existing checks; CLAUDE.md names `mise run test` as the unit test command.
acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's checks pass: existing unit tests (go test ./cmd/..., i.e. mise run test), including the existing trust_test.go and doctor_test.go cases.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 2: "can you create a windows docker container and try?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant attempts to verify the fix in a Windows Docker container (or clearly equivalent Windows execution environment) and reports the outcome honestly, including when it is not achievable on the host, without claiming Windows execution that did not happen.

acceptance_criteria.source: The change must compile at every call site and not break the repository's existing checks; CLAUDE.md lists golangci-lint as the linter.
acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's checks pass: the project builds (go build ./...) and golangci-lint reports no issues on the changed packages.
A pull request containing the fix is opened against entireio/cli, or the assistant reports that it cannot be opened from this environment and says why.
A comment linking the pull request is posted on issue entireio/cli#1761, or the assistant reports that it cannot post it and says why.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 3: "will be raised as saiprasannasastry right?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant answers the user's question about which GitHub account publishes the PR and comment, and ensures they are published as saiprasannasastry (or tells the user if that cannot be ensured).

analysis.completion_evidence: Turn 0 reply gave the issue summary and code trace; turn 1 reply was a plan with no tool calls; final diff replaces the regex with toml.Unmarshal in trust.go, adds single-quoted, escaped-backslash, dotted, malformed and no-state tests, updates doctor.go/lifecycle.go call sites and go.mod; test runs show all new codex and doctor tests PASS; the assistant reported the Windows container attempts (qemu/Rosetta/arm64 Wine) all failed and said so honestly; final turn reports PR https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1803 and an issue comment created after switching gh to saiprasannasastry.
analysis.notes: Turn 2 is ambiguous: the user only said 'create a windows docker container and try?' but the assistant interpreted it as permission to implement the fix plus attempt Windows verification; the user did not object. A true Windows Docker container is impossible on macOS, so c6 is about an honest attempt/report. c8 depends on external GitHub side effects not visible in the diff. The strategy-package flake mentioned was unrelated to the change.
analysis.task_statement: Starting from GitHub issue entireio/cli#1761 (Codex hook trust detector ignores single-quoted TOML state keys on Windows), the user asked for an explanation of the issue with a code trace, then a plan for implementing and sandbox-testing a fix, then asked the assistant to implement and try to verify it in a Windows Docker container, and finally to raise a PR and link it from an issue comment under the saiprasannasastry GitHub account.
